title: Jonah and the Atlas
premise: In the port town of Greyharbour, Tamsin Vane — a pearl diver's child indentured to the Meridian Trading Company — survives by being useful and invisible. When the army requisitions the town, the company, and its ledgers, Tamsin realizes the ledger holds proof that the company drowned divers for insurance money, including their mother. With the help of an aging clerk called the Atlas, who memorized every page, Tamsin races to get testimony on record before the victors' historians seal the archives. They succeed at terrible cost: the Atlas dies giving his deposition, but Tamsin's name — their real one — is entered into the official history, and they walk out of Greyharbour no longer property, but a witness.
about_author: Marguerite Sterling is the pen name of a former maritime archivist who spent a decade cataloguing colonial trading-company records. They write historical fiction about the people the ledgers reduced to line items.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Names
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. We meet Greyharbour through Tamsin's daily labor: diving, mending nets, copying ledger entries for the clerk they call the Atlas, who remembers every name. Tamsin hides their mother's death record in a loose floorboard. Emotional beat: quiet, watchful longing — Tamsin wants a life that is more than useful. Ends with warships appearing on the horizon.

chapters.title: Requisition
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The army seizes the town and the company's ledgers as evidence of company crimes — but officers plan to burn the diver records as irrelevant. The Atlas reveals he memorized the whole ledger and asks Tamsin to help him testify. Tamsin, terrified of being noticed, refuses. Emotional beat: fear versus conscience; Tamsin watches a diver's widow plead and is turned away.

chapters.title: What the Atlas Carried
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, climax. The Atlas is arrested for 'obstruction' when he attempts to speak to the historians. Tamsin breaks into the requisitioned archive with the widow's help, retrieves the hidden death record, and confronts the historian — offering the Atlas's testimony and the physical page together. Soldiers close in; the Atlas, released to verify the record, gives his deposition as the archive is sealed. Emotional beat: Tamsin chooses witness over survival-by-invisibility.

chapters.title: Entered into the Record
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The Atlas dies days after his deposition, and the historians — pressed by the widow's testimony and the page in Tamsin's hand — enter the divers' names into the official account. Tamsin's indenture is voided with the company's dissolution. They give the historian their mother's full name, then their own. Emotional beat: grief braided with belonging; Tamsin leaves Greyharbour with found family, carrying the Atlas's spare spectacles.
